newsitem.title: NEPAL: Two killed in Nepal clashes with Maoists.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Nepal clashes with Maoists.

text.p: Two people were killed and 13 injured in a clash between political party workers and hardline communist insurgents in a remote village in western Nepal, officials said on Tuesday.

They said the incident took place on Sunday in Rolpa district when workers of Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand's Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), campaigning ahead of local polls, were attacked by Maoists.
A spokesman for the Home (interior) Ministry said one RPP activist and an insurgent were killed. Four injured RPP workers were flown by helicopter to Kathmandu for treatment.
Nepal is holding elections on May 17 and 26 for 4,000 village committees that are the Himalayan kingdom's equivalent of local government.

A hardline faction of the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoists) is opposed to multi-party democracy and is boycotting the elections. The latest killing takes the death toll to five in election-related violence.
Overall about 100 people have been killed since the insurgency was launched 15 months ago in nine remote and poor districts of Nepal.
The Maoists, who are seeking to replace the parliamentary system with a government of the "working class", are not outlawed in Nepal but have said government offers of talks are not serious.
A multi-party system was established in Nepal in 1990 following pro-democracy demonstrations that whittled down the king's absolute powers.
